provenance.purpose: Frozen finder index the atlas-flows v4 FlowFinderQuery replays run against (UXP-617-1)
provenance.source: docs/product-truth/flows/**/*.flow.json and docs/reference/artifact-knowledge-graph.graph.json at that commit; screen titles from docs/product-truth/mockups/**/*.mockup.json at that commit
provenance.builder: buildFinderIndex() in leafcutter-web/lib/flow-finder/build-index.ts, fed by getFlows() and getScreenTitles() with LEAFCUTTER_REPO_ROOT pointing at an extract of that commit
provenance.regenerate: Do not regenerate from the live store: it grows. Rebuild only from a new measurement commit and update the dataset with it.

nodes.label: Review order
nodes.text: The customer sees a final summary of the plant, quantity, unit price and total before entering any payment details.

nodes.label: Enter payment
nodes.text: The customer enters their card details, which creates an authorized payment for this order, tied to their account and waiting to be captured.

nodes.label: Authorize & capture
nodes.text: The payment processor authorizes the card and the shop captures the payment, turning the open cart into a paid order linked to that payment.

nodes.label: Order confirmed
nodes.text: The customer sees a confirmation with the order number, the paid items and the amount captured.

nodes.label: Payment declined
nodes.text: The shop records the declined payment, places no order, keeps the cart and shows the customer a clear error with a way to try another payment method.
nodes.condition: the processor declines the card

nodes.label: Sold out at payment
nodes.text: The shop blocks authorization before anything is captured, creates no order and tells the customer the plant is no longer available.
nodes.condition: the plant dropped to zero stock after it was added to the cart

nodes.label: Browse plants
nodes.text: The customer browses the whole plant catalogue as a grid of cards showing each plant's name, photo, price and stock badge.

nodes.label: Plant detail
nodes.text: The customer opens one plant to see its photo, price and stock, and can add it to the cart.

nodes.label: Add to cart
nodes.text: The customer adds the plant to their cart and reviews what they are about to buy before paying.

nodes.label: Sign in
nodes.text: Before paying, the customer signs in or creates an account so the order is tied to them, and their cart is kept through sign-in.

nodes.label: Checkout
nodes.text: The customer confirms their details and pays in the checkout sub-journey, and an order is created.

nodes.label: Order confirmed
nodes.text: The customer sees a confirmation with the order number and what they bought.

nodes.label: Notify me
nodes.text: The shop replaces the 'Add to cart' button with a 'Notify me' button so the customer can be emailed when the plant is back.
nodes.condition: plant is out of stock

nodes.label: Empty cart
nodes.text: The customer opens an empty cart and sees an empty-cart message with a link back to the catalogue instead of a total and a pay button.
nodes.condition: the cart has no items

nodes.label: Payment declined
nodes.text: The shop places no order, keeps the cart intact and shows the customer a clear error with a way to try a different payment method.
nodes.condition: the payment is declined

nodes.label: Sold out at checkout
nodes.text: The shop blocks payment, creates no order and tells the customer the plant is no longer available.
nodes.condition: the plant sold out after it was added to the cart

nodes.label: My orders
nodes.text: The customer sees a list of their past orders with each order's number, item, total and status.

nodes.label: Order detail
nodes.text: The customer opens one order to see its item, quantity, total, payment status and date.

nodes.label: Track shipment
nodes.text: The customer sees the order's current delivery stage, with the carrier, the tracking number and whether the parcel is shipped, in transit or delivered.

nodes.label: No orders yet
nodes.text: A customer who has never ordered sees a friendly empty state inviting them to browse the catalogue instead of an empty table.
nodes.condition: the customer has no orders

nodes.label: Tracking not available yet
nodes.text: The customer sees that the paid order has not shipped yet and that tracking will appear once it is on its way, instead of a fake delivery stage.
nodes.condition: the order is paid but not yet dispatched (stage 'not-shipped', no tracking number)

nodes.label: Triage the request
nodes.text: A fast triage agent classifies your request as strategic, behavioral, technical or already covered and checks the store for duplicates before any criteria are written.

nodes.label: Author the AC tree (PO → BA → IT PO)
nodes.text: In turn, the product owner, business analyst and IT product owner agents write the acceptance criteria into the store, from value to behaviors to technical detail.

nodes.label: Review, approve & commit each stage
nodes.text: You approve each authoring stage before the next agent runs, which advances the criteria's readiness and commits that stage's output to Git.

nodes.label: Scan the store for ready work
nodes.text: The scanner finds the unblocked leaf acceptance criteria that are ready to build and presents them as a prioritized backlog of what to build next.

nodes.label: Generate a wired ticket
nodes.text: For a chosen ready criterion, the generator produces a fully wired ticket and links the two so the ticket and the criterion point at each other.

nodes.label: Implement, then mark the AC done
nodes.text: Once the implementing ticket merges, the system automatically marks every acceptance criterion that ticket covered as done.

nodes.label: Scope stays locked to the author
nodes.text: The checker lets implementation agents report progress but not rewrite the criteria, so only the author can change what done means and every change is traceable.
nodes.condition: an implementation agent tries to change an AC's scope

nodes.label: Discover & link existing code
nodes.text: The audit matches the existing code to the criterion by its exact text and links them, instead of generating a duplicate ticket.
nodes.condition: code for an AC already exists

nodes.label: Re-home without breaking links
nodes.text: The re-home tool moves the criterion to another component in a single change, and its permanent id keeps every existing reference working.
nodes.condition: the AC tree is reorganized

nodes.label: Retire & reconcile the code
nodes.text: The retire check confirms that the code a retired criterion claimed is actually gone, so a deprecated requirement cannot quietly leave live code behind.
nodes.condition: a requirement is retired

nodes.label: Classify what the request needs
nodes.text: The classifier agent reads the plain-language request and decides which of flow, mock data and mockups it needs, plus the target component and entities.

nodes.label: Search the store (add vs create)
nodes.text: Before drafting, the authoring agent searches the product-truth store by component and entities to decide whether to extend an existing artifact or create one.

nodes.label: Mock-data agent drafts the data
nodes.text: The mock-data agent drafts or extends the one canonical dataset of realistic records for the classified entities, which the mockups and flow are built on.

nodes.label: Mockup agent draws the screens
nodes.text: The mockup agent draws each screen the request implies, filled from the drafted mock data, and registers each screen so the flow's steps can point to it.

nodes.label: Flow agent assembles the journey
nodes.text: The flow agent assembles the draft flow, ordering the steps and linking each to its screen, the entities it reads and writes, and an acceptance scenario.

nodes.label: Business-analyst derives the ACs
nodes.text: After the person approves the draft flow, the business analyst agent derives acceptance criteria from its steps and links each step back to them.

nodes.label: Skip the flow agent
nodes.text: For a single-screen change, the classifier agent runs only the mock-data and mockup agents, skipping the flow agent since there is no journey.
nodes.condition: classifier outcome = mockup+data (a single screen, not a journey)

nodes.label: Only the mock-data agent runs
nodes.text: For backend logic, an API or a batch job, the classifier agent runs only the mock-data agent so tests get realistic fixtures, with no mockups or flow.
nodes.condition: classifier outcome = mock-data-only (backend/API/job, no screen)

nodes.label: Only the mockup agent runs
nodes.text: For a static screen with no business data, such as an About page, the classifier agent runs only the mockup agent, with no dataset or journey to draft.
nodes.condition: classifier outcome = mockup-only (a static screen with no records)

nodes.label: Draft no artifacts
nodes.text: For a configuration, schema, performance or documentation change, the classifier agent drafts nothing and the request goes straight to normal criteria authoring.
nodes.condition: classifier outcome = none (config / schema / docs, no product surface)

nodes.label: Mine repeat questions
nodes.text: An offline mining job reads published decisions and every kernel run in Langfuse, failed or unpublished ones included, and proposes recurring questions as candidate categories.

nodes.label: Suggest groupings
nodes.text: An AI model suggests grouping wordings that ask the same thing into one category with a preferred wording, optionally under a broader category, as a suggestion only.

nodes.label: Approve a category
nodes.text: You review each suggested category with its wordings and where they were seen, then accept, change or undo it, and only your approval turns it into a category.

nodes.label: Stage the record
nodes.text: The kernel writes the approved category beside the run that approved it, never into the repository.

nodes.label: Publish to the library
nodes.text: You publish the staged category, which is checked, added to the criteria library and reviewed and merged like any other change, while decision records stay unedited.

nodes.label: Count usage from the records
nodes.text: A generated, freshness-checked index counts how many published decisions used each category, never treating frequent use as proof that a category is good.

nodes.label: Keep outcomes as Neo4j aggregates
nodes.text: Where a Neo4j learning store is set up, the system rebuilds how each category's decisions turned out as aggregates, kept out of Git and out of what is offered.

nodes.label: Import categories into the knowledge graph
nodes.text: After publish, the knowledge importer reads the published categories and adds each one, its replacement links and its memberships to the next knowledge graph generation.

nodes.label: Explore which decisions share which questions
nodes.text: You ask the graph which categories a decision's criteria used and which decisions used a category, and follow a question across every decision that asked it.

nodes.label: Merge, split or retire categories
nodes.text: Later you merge, split or retire published categories through the same stage and publish path, keeping ids, moving members to the replacement and leaving decisions untouched.

nodes.label: Reject or undo: nothing staged
nodes.text: Your rejection leaves the candidate as a proposal or drops it, so nothing is staged and no published category changes.
nodes.condition: you reject the candidate or undo its suggested grouping

nodes.label: No learning store: outcomes off
nodes.text: Outcome statistics are simply switched off, while usage counts, reuse and every decision work exactly the same.
nodes.condition: no Neo4j learning store is configured, or LEAFCUTTER_SELF_LEARNING is false

nodes.label: Import fails: graph unchanged
nodes.text: The importer does not publish the new generation, keeps the active graph as it was and names the failing record, changing nothing in Git.
nodes.condition: a category record fails validation, for example a member names a criterion its decision does not carry, or the build fails

nodes.label: Change it in the record, not the graph
nodes.text: You make the change in the category record and take it through stage and publish, and the next graph generation shows it, because the graph is only a rebuildable view.
nodes.condition: you want to rename, merge, split or retire a category you found in the graph

nodes.label: Ask the question
nodes.text: You ask the host a question, and it passes your exact words and any context you supplied to the kernel.

nodes.label: Recognize repository terms
nodes.text: The kernel recognizes glossary terms, artifact types, symbols and ids in your question and adds their short meanings, marking what it cannot recognize, before intent is classified.

nodes.label: Classify the intent
nodes.text: Jev classifies the intent of your unchanged question using the term meanings and your context, asking you only when the intent stays unclear or a choice is needed.

nodes.label: Spot a compound subject
nodes.text: At routing, Jev judges whether the subject bundles several separate questions, and if it does, the kernel offers a split whatever routing concluded about it.

nodes.label: Propose the parts
nodes.text: Claude Code proposes two to five parts, each quoting the words of the subject it covers, naming the parts it waits for and saying whether a decision or research runs it.

nodes.label: Approve the split
nodes.text: You see the subject, each proposed part with its quote, dependencies and capability, and any dropped proposal, then approve, edit, pick some or reject before anything runs.

nodes.label: Run the parts in order
nodes.text: The kernel runs the approved parts one at a time in dependency order as children of this run, each as a decision or research, with earlier results as precedent for later ones.

nodes.label: Check for precedent
nodes.text: The kernel looks up earlier published decisions that might apply and has each one judged for fit, as the precedent flow shows.

nodes.label: Ground it in the repository
nodes.text: Research retrieves evidence from the repository with exact locations, and Jev reranks it and, for a question about the project graph, picks which offered query to run.

nodes.label: Synthesize the findings
nodes.text: Claude Code writes findings that cite only the retrieved evidence.

nodes.label: Start from approved categories
nodes.text: The kernel first offers the approved criterion categories that fit this decision's kind and components, in their preferred wording, as proposals you still approve.

nodes.label: Judge what the reused criteria miss
nodes.text: Jev judges whether the reused criteria miss anything this decision needs, and its verdict goes to the approval gate so you see why new criteria were or were not drafted.

nodes.label: Propose options and criteria
nodes.text: Claude Code proposes options beside the reused criteria, keeping options you named as yours, and drafts new criteria only when Jev found a gap or no category fits.

nodes.label: Approve the proposals
nodes.text: You review the proposed and reused options and criteria with Jev's gap verdict, and nothing is used until you approve all, some or with a condition, edit criteria or add options.

nodes.label: Research the options' claims
nodes.text: A targeted research round checks the claims the approved options make, reads the files they cite and looks into open gaps, with Jev ranking and judging the evidence.

nodes.label: Assess every option
nodes.text: Jev judges every option against every criterion for fit and enough evidence, and marks each criterion as answerable by evidence or a design judgement.

nodes.label: Make the ranked choice
nodes.text: You see the options ranked by Jev's scores and why research stopped, then choose one, choose one with a condition, add an option or answer in your own words.

nodes.label: Resolve the decision
nodes.text: The kernel resolves the decision as approved by you, writes the report to the run folder and keeps any condition you stated word for word in every later rationale and the record.

nodes.label: Report the split
nodes.text: The kernel reports where each part stands, whether pending, decided, answered or not run, linking its decision record or research result, with one line per part in the run report.

nodes.label: Continue with honest limits
nodes.text: The kernel records partial coverage, unresolved references and what it left out, then classifies within those limits without a broad search or asking you about unknown terms.
nodes.condition: the scoped entity index is missing, stale or partly unsupported, a reference is ambiguous or unknown, recognition is disabled, or a configured bound is reached

nodes.label: Revise before approving
nodes.text: Only what you approved, edited or added goes on to research and assessment, and words you write are kept as your input, never turned into criteria.
nodes.condition: you approve only some proposals, edit the criteria, or add options

nodes.label: Ask early, on limited evidence
nodes.text: The kernel asks you early with the last complete ranking, plainly marked as made on limited evidence.
nodes.condition: another research round and a final assessment no longer fit in the Jev call budget

nodes.label: Research before asking what is missing
nodes.text: Instead of asking you what is missing, the kernel first runs its one targeted research round on open gaps, added claims and cited files, then has the options assessed again.
nodes.condition: Jev names no missing evidence, conflict or missing option (an unidentified gap) while usable options exist, and a targeted research round is due

nodes.label: Ranked question instead of a blind one
nodes.text: The kernel asks you the ranked choice question rather than a blind question about what is missing, stating why research stopped and keeping that reason with the decision.
nodes.condition: Jev names no missing evidence, conflict or missing option (an unidentified gap) while usable options exist, and no targeted research round is due

nodes.label: Rule on an escalation
nodes.text: The kernel asks you directly, offering the tied or usable options and free text, and the option you choose resolves the decision as your ruling, keeping any condition you add.
nodes.condition: the assessment ends in an escalation that is not a ranked question: a tie, an unstated preference, a conflict or an uncertainty that synthesis could not settle, so you are asked directly (phase awaiting_human) with usable options as choices

nodes.label: Assess and rank again
nodes.text: The kernel has the options assessed and ranked again with what you added, your own words counting as a stated constraint, before asking you again.
nodes.condition: you add an option or answer in your own words instead of choosing

nodes.label: No answer, no record
nodes.text: The decision never resolves, so no record is staged and nothing reaches the decision store.
nodes.condition: you never answer or you cancel the run

nodes.label: One question, no split
nodes.text: The kernel splits nothing, and the run goes on as one decision from the precedent step.
nodes.condition: the subject is a single question and routing finds one capability for it

nodes.label: One question, no capability
nodes.text: The kernel shows no split gate, records the missing capability and ends the run blocked, exactly as without splitting.
nodes.condition: the subject is a single question and routing finds no capability for it

nodes.label: Typed request, never split
nodes.text: The kernel never checks a typed decision request for bundling and runs it as the one decision the caller named.
nodes.condition: the caller supplied a decision request (leafcutter.decision_request.v1) that names its own question, options and criteria

nodes.label: Split found mid-run
nodes.text: The kernel starts the same split for that work item, recording that it was found mid-run, and sends it to the same approval gate.
nodes.condition: a work item below the root holds a multi-part decision question or a research request with several needs

nodes.label: Drop a part with no quote
nodes.text: The kernel drops that proposal before you see it and shows it read-only with its reason, so it cannot run unless you add its question with an edit.
nodes.condition: a proposed part's quote is not found in the subject

nodes.label: Fewer than two parts
nodes.text: The kernel shows no gate and treats the request as one question, so it ends blocked, asks for clarification or goes ahead as one, depending on why the split was offered.
nodes.condition: the proposal holds fewer than 2 parts, also when counted after parts whose quote is not in the subject are set aside; what follows depends on why the split was offered (trigger jev_none, trigger ambiguous, or trigger bundled_accepted or found mid-run)

nodes.label: More than five parts
nodes.text: The kernel offers the first five parts at the gate and lists the rest read-only with their quotes as not covered, to be asked again as a separate request.
nodes.condition: more than 5 parts are proposed

nodes.label: Edit or pick a subset
nodes.text: An edited part runs with your words while the record keeps the proposed text, an unticked part is recorded as left out and never runs, and at least one part stays in.
nodes.condition: you edit a part's text or untick some parts before approving

nodes.label: Reject, run ends blocked
nodes.text: No part runs, the kernel records the capability gap and ends the run blocked, and the report says the split was rejected and suggests asking one bounded question.
nodes.condition: you reject a split offered because no capability matched the subject (trigger jev_none)

nodes.label: Reject, ask today's clarification
nodes.text: No part runs and the kernel falls back to its usual clarification question, so the run waits for your answer instead of ending blocked and the report notes the rejected split.
nodes.condition: you reject a split offered because routing could not choose one capability for the subject (trigger ambiguous: insufficient_context, reason jev_needs_context or low_confidence)

nodes.label: Reject, keep it whole
nodes.text: No part runs, and the kernel lets the subject go ahead as one decision or research step without blocking, noting the rejected split in the report.
nodes.condition: you reject a split offered for a subject routing would have accepted as one (trigger bundled_accepted), or for a work item found mid-run

nodes.label: A part does not settle
nodes.text: The kernel shows the part as not settled with the reason, skips parts that wait for it, runs the rest, and ends the run partial rather than completed.
nodes.condition: an approved part runs but does not settle (budget stop, blocked, capability gap or cancelled)

nodes.label: No category fits: frame it as today
nodes.text: The kernel reuses nothing and judges no gap, so options and criteria are proposed as usual and an empty library never blocks or slows a decision.
nodes.condition: no published category fits the decision's kind and components, including when the library is still empty

nodes.label: Draft criteria for the gap only
nodes.text: Claude Code drafts new criteria for that gap alone beside the reused ones, and you can still add your own at the approval gate.
nodes.condition: Jev finds that the reused criteria leave out something this decision needs

nodes.label: Form the decision
nodes.text: You ask a question, and the kernel uses short meanings of its terms to classify the intent, gathers evidence, weighs the options and asks you to approve and choose.

nodes.label: Stage the record
nodes.text: When the run ends, the kernel saves the approved decision as a record in the run folder, never in the repository, and tells you where publishing writes it and how to publish.

nodes.label: Publish the record
nodes.text: You run the printed publish command, which checks the record and writes it with a regenerated index into the decision folder, and the change then goes through a normal Git review.

nodes.label: Reuse it as precedent
nodes.text: A later decision run finds the record through the index, Jev judges whether it applies, and a strong match asks you to reuse it or decide anew.

nodes.label: Decide to publish
nodes.text: You decide to publish by running the command the staging notice printed, from any shell and folder, or by asking Claude Code to run it and open a pull request.

nodes.label: Validate the staged record
nodes.text: The publish command checks the staged record's structure and links, and that its components and roadmap phase appear in the project's component list and roadmap.

nodes.label: Write the record and the index
nodes.text: The publish command writes the record into the decision folder of the kernel checkout and regenerates the decision index.

nodes.label: Validate the store
nodes.text: The validate command checks the whole decision store and reports any problems it finds.

nodes.label: Commit and review in git
nodes.text: The new record and index are committed, and a pull request is opened and reviewed like any other change, because Git is the canonical store.

nodes.label: Merge to main
nodes.text: The pull request merges to main, and from then on every later run working from that revision can find the record.

nodes.label: Keep it staged
nodes.text: The record stays only in the run folder, so later runs, which look up precedent through the published index, never find it.
nodes.condition: you choose not to publish

nodes.label: Exit 3: no staged record
nodes.text: The publish command stops with an error naming the run, writes no file and leaves the index untouched.
nodes.condition: the run has no staged decision record

nodes.label: Exit 3: unknown filter value
nodes.text: The publish command stops, names the unknown component or roadmap phase, and writes nothing until the record uses known values.
nodes.condition: a component or roadmap phase on the record is not in docs/components.json or docs/roadmap.json

nodes.label: Correct an older record
nodes.text: The publish command marks the older record as corrected and superseded by the new one, keeps its original choice, evidence and assumptions, and rewrites it in one safe step.
nodes.condition: you pass --correct OLD_ID for an older record that the new record supersedes

nodes.label: Look up matching records
nodes.text: The kernel searches the decision index for earlier records that match the new decision's components and roadmap phase, scores them by text and checks each file is unchanged.

nodes.label: Ask Jev whether each applies
nodes.text: Jev judges, for up to three candidate records, whether each earlier decision applies here, asking once before options exist and then alongside the option assessment.

nodes.label: Cite it as evidence
nodes.text: The kernel turns a precedent scoring 0.5 or more into evidence that cites the earlier record and who approved it.

nodes.label: Reuse it, or decide anew?
nodes.text: When a precedent scores 0.8 or more, is not superseded and the decision has no options of its own, you are asked whether to reuse it or decide anew.

nodes.label: Reuse the earlier choice
nodes.text: The kernel resolves the decision with the earlier choice, approved by you, and stages a new record that cites the precedent.

nodes.label: Does not apply
nodes.text: The kernel leaves the earlier decision out, and the new decision carries on without it.
nodes.condition: Jev scores the precedent below 0.5

nodes.label: Evidence only, no reuse question
nodes.text: The kernel keeps the precedent as cited evidence and the normal forming flow continues without interrupting you.
nodes.condition: the score is below 0.8, the new decision already has options, or the precedent is superseded

nodes.label: Decide anew
nodes.text: The normal forming flow continues with the precedent kept as evidence, and if you end up choosing differently the new record supersedes the old one.
nodes.condition: you choose to decide anew

nodes.label: Spot an approved decision
nodes.text: At the end of the run, the kernel spots a completed decision that a person approved.

nodes.label: Build the record
nodes.text: The kernel builds a record of the question, options, criteria, evidence references, the ranking you saw, precedents and provenance, refusing it unless a person approved it.

nodes.label: Write it under the run folder
nodes.text: The kernel writes the record into the run folder, never into the repository, which a run only ever reads.

nodes.label: Tell you how to publish
nodes.text: Claude Code tells you the decision record is staged, which folder publishing writes it into and a publish command that runs as printed, and never publishes on its own.

nodes.label: Nothing is staged
nodes.text: The kernel writes no record, so there is nothing to publish and no later run can find this decision as precedent.
nodes.condition: the decision was resolved by the host alone or has no human approval

nodes.label: Say what you want
nodes.text: The person describes the feature they want in plain language, with no spec format or Gherkin, just their intent.

nodes.label: Classify what to draft
nodes.text: An AI agent reads the request and decides which artifacts it needs, from a full journey to a single screen or a dataset, plus the component and entities involved.

nodes.label: Draft the mock data
nodes.text: For anything data-backed, an AI agent drafts or extends the one canonical mock-data set for those entities, the realistic records the draft builds on.

nodes.label: Draft the mockups
nodes.text: For each screen the request implies, an AI agent drafts a mockup filled from that mock data, so the person sees real-looking screens rather than a description.

nodes.label: Assemble the draft flow
nodes.text: An AI agent assembles the steps into a draft flow, linking each to its screen and the entities it reads and writes, as a reviewable map of the journey.

nodes.label: You review & approve; ACs are generated
nodes.text: The person reviews the draft flow with its mock data and mockups and approves it, and acceptance criteria are then generated from the flow's steps.

nodes.label: Plan
nodes.text: You say what you want and AI agents author the acceptance criteria for it.

nodes.label: Build
nodes.text: AI phase agents drive the wired ticket through its build phases until it is green and committed.

nodes.label: Finalize
nodes.text: The finalize pipeline merges the pull request and closes the epic or ticket.

nodes.label: Open the Flows view
nodes.text: The person opens the Flows view and sees the list of flows that match the current source, kind and realization filters.

nodes.label: Choose source (mock/real) and kind (user/data/architecture)
nodes.text: The person filters the loaded flows by source, kind and realization, and the visible list updates at once without saving anything.

nodes.label: Select a flow to render its graph
nodes.text: The person picks one of the filtered flows and Atlas draws its graph.

nodes.label: Open a step to see its ACs' live status + mock records + mockup
nodes.text: The person opens a step's drawer to see the live status of its acceptance criteria, its inputs and outputs with examples, and the mock records and mockup it uses.

nodes.label: Jump from an AC to the flows it appears in
nodes.text: From an acceptance criterion's details, the person follows a link to each flow step or branch where that criterion appears.

nodes.label: 'Appears in flows' links open the step itself
nodes.text: Each 'Appears in flows' link in the criterion's drawer points at the step or branch that realizes the criterion, using its flow's own address with that step named.

nodes.label: Open a flow from its canonical link
nodes.text: When someone opens a flow's own address, Atlas shows that flow selected and drawn, with filters set to match it, no drawer open and a breadcrumb naming only that flow.

nodes.label: Open a step link with its drawer open
nodes.text: When someone opens a step link, Atlas shows the flow as for a flow link with the named step's or branch's drawer already open, keeping the step in the address.

nodes.label: Opening a drawer writes ?step= in place
nodes.text: When the person opens a step's or branch's drawer, Atlas rewrites the address in place to name that step without adding a Back entry, even from the bare Flows page.

nodes.label: Closing the drawer removes ?step= in place
nodes.text: When the person closes the drawer, Atlas removes the step from the address in place, leaving the flow's own address and adding no Back entry.

nodes.label: Select, drill and breadcrumb push the flow's URL
nodes.text: Picking a flow, drilling into a sub-flow or clicking a breadcrumb makes Atlas add a history entry with the target flow's address, while filter changes never add one.

nodes.label: Back and Forward move between flows
nodes.text: The browser's Back and Forward buttons move between flow entries, and Atlas restores each one's address, flow, breadcrumb trail, open drawer and filters as they were left.

nodes.label: Filter change re-picks the flow: address replaced
nodes.text: Atlas draws the first flow the new filters list, with a fresh breadcrumb and no drawer, and replaces the current address with that flow's address without adding a Back entry.
nodes.condition: the new Source, Kind or Realization filters no longer include the entry flow

nodes.label: Filter change keeps the flow: address unchanged
nodes.text: Atlas leaves the drawn flow, the breadcrumb trail, any open drawer and the address exactly as they were, adding no Back entry.
nodes.condition: the new Source, Kind or Realization filters still include the entry flow

nodes.label: Bare /flows keeps its address
nodes.text: Atlas keeps the plain Flows address and draws the default flow with the default filters and a breadcrumb naming only that flow.
nodes.condition: the address is the bare /flows, with no flow id

nodes.label: Flow not found (404)
nodes.text: Atlas answers with a 404 Flow not found notice that quotes the requested id and links back to the Flows view, drawing no flow and keeping the bad address to correct.
nodes.condition: the flow id in the address names no flow

nodes.label: Step not found
nodes.text: Atlas opens the flow as usual but with no drawer, and shows a Step not found notice quoting the unknown step until the person opens a real one.
nodes.condition: the ?step= value names no step or branch of the flow

nodes.label: Open a real step after 'Step not found'
nodes.text: Atlas clears the Step not found notice and replaces the unknown step in the address with the opened one, in place and without adding a Back entry.
nodes.condition: the link's ?step= named no step or branch, and the person then opens a real step's or branch's drawer

nodes.label: Legacy ?flow= link redirects (308)
nodes.text: Atlas permanently redirects the old-style link to the matching step link, opening that flow with the step's drawer open and leaving the old address out of the history.
nodes.condition: the link is a legacy /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> link

nodes.label: Switch from one drawer to another
nodes.text: Atlas swaps the open drawer for the newly clicked one and replaces the step in the address in place, so only one drawer and one step are ever shown.
nodes.condition: another step's or branch's drawer is already open

nodes.label: Leave a flow while its drawer is open
nodes.text: Atlas closes the drawer and adds a history entry for the target flow with no step, while the entry left behind keeps its open step so Back returns to it.
nodes.condition: a step's or branch's drawer is open when the person selects or drills

nodes.label: Pre-merge baseline
nodes.text: The test agent captures a test baseline on main before merging, so later failures can be triaged against a known-good starting point.

nodes.label: Open the PR
nodes.text: The pull request agent opens a pull request for the branch if one does not already exist.

nodes.label: Merge origin/main in
nodes.text: The finalize pipeline merges the latest main into the feature worktree and halts on a conflict instead of advancing.

nodes.label: Post-merge tests + triage
nodes.text: The test agents run the post-merge suite and triage any failures against the baseline, halting on a real regression.

nodes.label: Close tickets + ACs
nodes.text: The finalize pipeline closes the tickets and marks their source acceptance criteria done in the store.

nodes.label: Merge the PR to main
nodes.text: After the person confirms, the finalize pipeline merges the pull request into the protected main branch.

nodes.label: Archive + remove worktree
nodes.text: Once the pull request is merged, AI agents archive the epic and remove the feature worktree.

nodes.label: Read and normalize the stored flow JSON
nodes.text: Atlas reads every stored flow, turns each readable one into the shape its views draw, and adds the artifact knowledge graph as an architecture view.

nodes.label: Resolve each step to its AC's live work_status
nodes.text: Atlas gives each step and branch the live work status of its linked acceptance criteria, keeping the stored status for unknown criteria and never changing the criteria.

nodes.label: Draw the graph on the /flows page
nodes.text: Atlas passes the flows, their mock records and screen titles to the Flows page, which draws each flow as a graph and shows each step's inputs and outputs in its drawer.

nodes.label: Build the AC work_status map
nodes.text: The generator reads the acceptance criteria store once and builds a map of each criterion's work status for every later step to use.

nodes.label: Derive each step's impl_status and roll up impl_summary
nodes.text: The generator recomputes each step's and branch's build status from its linked acceptance criteria and totals those statuses into a summary for the flow.

nodes.label: Invert flow->AC edges into the by_ac index
nodes.text: The generator turns the flow-to-criterion links around into an index from each acceptance criterion to its flow steps, and rebuilds the component, entity and flow indexes.

nodes.label: Write the product_truth back-ref onto each AC
nodes.text: The generator rewrites each linked acceptance criterion's product-truth links to show which flow steps, screens and mock data realize it, leaving its authored text alone.

nodes.label: Fail on derived-vs-source drift
nodes.text: The validator recomputes every derived value and fails the run if any status, link, index, screen-to-mockup reference or declared step contract has drifted from its source.

nodes.label: Build driver dispatches phases
nodes.text: The build driver reads which phases the ticket needs and runs each needed phase agent in priority order, moving on according to the status each one signs off with.

nodes.label: Status check (prio 1)
nodes.text: The status agent reads the ticket's state, the current branch and any phases or commits already done, so the build starts from where things really are.

nodes.label: ADR (prio 2, conditional)
nodes.text: When the ticket calls for one, the decision record agent writes an architecture decision record for the change.

nodes.label: Architecture diagram (prio 3, conditional)
nodes.text: When the ticket calls for one, the diagram agent writes or updates the C4 architecture diagram for the change.

nodes.label: IT-PO enrichment (prio 3.5, conditional)
nodes.text: The IT product owner agent fills in the acceptance criteria's technical details, such as the assigned agent, contracts and complexity, if they still lack them.

nodes.label: Architect review (prio 4, conditional)
nodes.text: When a guardrail gate or the ticket calls for it, the architect agent rates how far the change reaches, notes or escalates it, and decides whether a decision record is needed.

nodes.label: Test-writer — TDD red (prio 5)
nodes.text: The test-writing agent writes failing tests from the ticket's test requirements as the red baseline the coders must turn green, skipping docs-only and config-only tickets.

nodes.label: Coders make it green (prio 6-8)
nodes.text: The Python, SQL and frontend coding agents change only the ticket's planned files until every test in the red baseline passes.

nodes.label: Test-runner (prio 9)
nodes.text: The test runner agent picks and runs the right test suite for what changed and reports whether the red baseline now passes.

nodes.label: Documentation (prio 10, conditional)
nodes.text: When the acceptance criteria or a flow-change gate call for it, the documentation agent writes or updates the docs, ahead of the coders on flow-change tickets.

nodes.label: Change-scope review (prio 10)
nodes.text: The scope review agent compares the staged changes with the ticket's planned files and flags each unexpected file as soft, hard or ambiguous.

nodes.label: PR self-review (prio 11)
nodes.text: The review agent checks the diff, keeps only high-confidence findings and escalates a cluster of medium-confidence ones to a stronger model before the coverage gates.

nodes.label: AC coverage gate (prio 11.5)
nodes.text: The coverage agent confirms that every acceptance criterion has real implementation and test evidence in the diff before the commit.

nodes.label: User-surface smoke (prio 11.5, conditional)
nodes.text: When the ticket declares a user-facing surface, the smoke test agent runs it end to end and checks its side effects.

nodes.label: AC fulfillment gate (prio 11.7)
nodes.text: The fulfillment agent checks the acceptance criteria store's status and links against the evidence and adds what is missing, so the store is accurate before commit.

nodes.label: Live-surface test (prio 11.8, conditional)
nodes.text: When the ticket asks for it, the live test agent starts a dev server, sends real HTTP requests to declared fixtures, checks the responses and shuts the server down.

nodes.label: Gated commit (prio 12)
nodes.text: The commit agent shows the planned message and files, commits them, and on a pre-commit hook failure fixes what it can and retries once.

nodes.label: Open the pull request (prio 13)
nodes.text: The pull request agent drafts the title and body from the branch's commits, opens or reuses the pull request and resolves merge conflicts, and its merge marks the criterion done.

nodes.label: Blocker → adjudication ladder
nodes.text: The supervisor climbs the failure ladder instead of advancing, from a mechanical retry to rework by another agent, a brainstorm and finally a halt, each with a retry cap.
nodes.condition: a phase agent signs off with status: blocker

nodes.label: Product-truth store lives beside the AC store
nodes.text: The product-truth store keeps flows, mock data and mockups right beside the acceptance criteria store it links into.

nodes.label: The Atlas reads it live and renders flows
nodes.text: Atlas reads the product-truth store and draws its flows, holding what it read until it is refreshed or restarted.

nodes.label: Agents produce & extend the artifacts
nodes.text: Leafcutter's AI agents draft flows, seed mock data and write acceptance criteria, keeping the product-truth layer alive.

nodes.label: Load conventions
nodes.text: The coding agent loads the project's conventions so its code matches the repository's error-handling, style and structure rules.

nodes.label: Implement against red
nodes.text: The coding agent edits only the files the ticket names, to make the failing tests handed over by the test-writing agent pass.

nodes.label: Doc-enforcer
nodes.text: The documentation enforcer checks the changed Python files against the project's docstring and documentation conventions.

nodes.label: Complexity reduction
nodes.text: The coding agent simplifies the new code to keep it within the repository's complexity budget.

nodes.label: Run until green
nodes.text: The test agent runs the suite until every test in the failing baseline passes.

nodes.label: Record sign-off
nodes.text: The coding agent records its sign-off, updating the ticket's status and its sign-off checklist together.

nodes.label: Start with the question
nodes.text: The caller asks a research question within the permitted project scope without choosing a retrieval operation.

nodes.label: Keep one source and scope
nodes.text: The system fixes the repository, the permitted sources and the published revision before work begins and keeps them unchanged through any pause.

nodes.label: Dispatch the information-needs request
nodes.text: The system gathers the permitted meanings of the question and asks the host model to interpret the information the answer needs.

nodes.label: Interpret all information needs together
nodes.text: The host model identifies the required facts and distinguishes acceptance behavior, authored verification checks and narrower requests without retrieving evidence.

nodes.label: Validate and carry the interpretation forward
nodes.text: The system validates the interpretation and carries its original targets and required facts forward, or requests a missing user choice.

nodes.label: Check whether the data can answer it
nodes.text: The system checks whether the source data has the needed kinds, relationships and fields, so missing data is never mistaken for a missing query.

nodes.label: Choose a registered query
nodes.text: Jev selects an offered operation for the interpreted need and permitted targets, whether or not a saved-query catalog is configured.

nodes.label: Bind and validate arguments
nodes.text: The system fills in the query's arguments from known, scoped and clarified values and checks them against the operation's contract.

nodes.label: Retrieve bounded, attributable evidence
nodes.text: The system retrieves bounded evidence from the pinned source and gives each requested source field its own citation.

nodes.label: Check exact coverage
nodes.text: The system checks every original target, required field and population against the returned evidence, keeping incomplete coverage and unknown totals explicit.

nodes.label: Judge research sufficiency
nodes.text: Jev judges whether the evidence meets the original need, though a positive verdict cannot erase missing facts or partial results.

nodes.label: Return the answer, limits and next step
nodes.text: The system returns the attributable evidence with an honest outcome, keeping the run waiting for a specific response or stopping when limits or unresolved facts block progress.

nodes.label: Direct lookup · no Jev
nodes.text: The system validates the typed request, runs the registered operation against a published revision and returns bounded evidence without involving Jev.
nodes.condition: The caller already knows the operation and arguments

nodes.label: Prepare native candidates
nodes.text: The system extracts search terms from the question and scores and merges a bounded pool of candidate matches.
nodes.condition: No explicit knowledge request and no eligible graph source

nodes.label: Conditionally judge native relevance
nodes.text: When data policy and budget allow, Jev judges which of the offered candidates are relevant to the question.
nodes.condition: No explicit knowledge request and no eligible graph source

nodes.label: Return native evidence
nodes.text: The system orders the candidates, falling back to term hits and marking relevance as unjudged where needed, and returns them with citations.
nodes.condition: No explicit knowledge request and no eligible graph source

nodes.label: Dispatch clarification
nodes.text: The system sends out a bounded clarification question and saves it with the original context so the run can resume later.
nodes.condition: Required facts, population or inputs are ambiguous

nodes.label: Answer clarification
nodes.text: The person answers the clarification question with the requested choice, without widening what the run is allowed to do.
nodes.condition: Required facts, population or inputs are ambiguous

nodes.label: Validate clarification resume
nodes.text: The system checks that the answer matches the waiting run and question, then resumes the run exactly once.
nodes.condition: Required facts, population or inputs are ambiguous

nodes.label: Disclose the data gap
nodes.text: The system leaves the requested fact unresolved and names only the data proven missing, never treating it as an empty result or a reason to build a query.
nodes.condition: Required source kinds, fields or mappings are absent or unknown

nodes.label: Author query candidate
nodes.text: The coding agent writes a bounded query recipe, with expected-result cases, from the scoped request.
nodes.condition: Data is supported, but no offered query meets the need

nodes.label: Verify and activate query
nodes.text: The system independently verifies the new query, checks permission to add it to the catalog, and resumes only with a verified version.
nodes.condition: Data is supported, but no offered query meets the need

nodes.label: Stop honestly, without fabricating zero results
nodes.text: The system reports that the query could not be served and why, without passing this off as an empty result or starting any indexing or catalog change.
nodes.condition: The source is stale, unavailable, denied or the budget is exhausted

nodes.label: Partial is an answer condition, not a success badge
nodes.text: The system keeps the evidence found, the missing facts and the unknown total, and continues only while useful work and budget remain, otherwise returning a partial result.
nodes.condition: Evidence or required fields remain incomplete

nodes.label: Keep the result; qualify observation
nodes.text: The system keeps the retrieval result, adds a cleaned-up warning instead of retrying, and claims an accessible trace only after the remote trace is verified.
nodes.condition: Tracing is disabled, fails or is not remotely verified

nodes.label: Request synthesis
nodes.text: The system saves a synthesis request with the evidence and limits and waits for the host model to answer it.
nodes.condition: Research needs a bounded host synthesis before finalizing

nodes.label: Synthesize findings
nodes.text: The host model writes findings based only on the evidence it was given.
nodes.condition: Research needs a bounded host synthesis before finalizing

nodes.label: Resume synthesis
nodes.text: The system checks that the host's response matches the waiting request and resumes the run, keeping any partial assessments.
nodes.condition: Research needs a bounded host synthesis before finalizing

nodes.label: Skip this retrieval need
nodes.text: After Jev's recorded skip, the system closes this need as blocked because no retrieval is needed, running no other query and claiming no answer.
nodes.condition: Jev selects the offered skip outcome

nodes.label: Prepare the question and offered meanings
nodes.text: The system validates the question, context and catalog of offered meanings within the size limit, adding as candidates only identifiers given or named in the question.

nodes.label: Start the isolated kernel run
nodes.text: The kernel starts an isolated run that allows exactly one host operation, with Jev calls, knowledge reads and memory turned off.

nodes.label: Save the request and wait for the host
nodes.text: The kernel saves the request and its input for the external host, then pauses the run until the host answers, without calling any model itself.

nodes.label: Interpret all information needs together
nodes.text: The host model uses the offered meanings to distinguish acceptance behavior, authored verification checks and narrower requests in one interpretation without retrieving evidence.

nodes.label: Submit the interpretation to its wait
nodes.text: The host controller wraps the interpretation for the original run and wait and submits it to the kernel, leaving unknown model or token usage unclaimed.

nodes.label: Check the response before accepting it
nodes.text: The kernel checks that the response fits the current wait and schema, keeps the question unchanged and uses only offered, non-overlapping labels, which proves form, not correctness.

nodes.label: Record acceptance and resume the run
nodes.text: The kernel records the accepted response in its durable ledger before resuming the run, so an identical replay changes nothing and a conflicting one is refused.

nodes.label: Normalize the interpretation
nodes.text: The kernel adds structural gaps to the unresolved reasons, marks the interpretation as decided or needing resolution, and records a model only if the host reported one.

nodes.label: Return the typed needs
nodes.text: The kernel returns the typed needs as a completed interpretation, which does not mean any retrieval or answer has happened.

nodes.label: Reject an invalid request
nodes.text: The system rejects the task before any host wait is created, without trimming the catalog, inventing targets or reinterpreting the question.
nodes.condition: Input is malformed, ungrounded or outside the request bounds

nodes.label: Keep waiting across a restart
nodes.text: The kernel keeps the saved wait open, even across a restart, so the original run resumes when a valid response finally arrives.
nodes.condition: The host has not submitted a response

nodes.label: Refuse the wrong submission
nodes.text: The kernel refuses the submission without recording it or changing the run, so the host must resend it correctly for the current wait.
nodes.condition: The wrapper, actor, run, wait, revision or response kind is invalid

nodes.label: Return to the host for correction
nodes.text: The kernel records the rejection and sends the request back to the host with the reasons, allowing one corrected response.
nodes.condition: The payload fails schema or request-bound validation and its first correction remains

nodes.label: Stop after correction fails
nodes.text: The kernel records the second rejection, fails the work item and closes the wait without accepting any response.
nodes.condition: A second payload fails schema or request-bound validation after the one allowed correction

nodes.label: Return unsupported or unresolved needs
nodes.text: The kernel keeps the question, the selected and uncertain values and the reasons, and returns the interpretation as needing resolution without asking anyone or searching.
nodes.condition: Valid output contains unresolved reasons or structural missing dimensions

nodes.label: Report a conversion failure
nodes.text: The kernel reports a failed result instead of a completed interpretation, even though the response was already accepted.
nodes.condition: Accepted submission cannot produce a valid normalized result

nodes.label: Decide whether a query is missing
nodes.text: Jev chooses to build a new query only when the source data is supported and none of the offered queries fits, without writing the request itself.

nodes.label: Construct the scoped request
nodes.text: The system assembles the original need, the input and output requirements and the source-fit evidence, skips duplicate builds and hands the request to the coding agent.

nodes.label: Build a candidate query
nodes.text: The coding agent writes a parameterized, bounded query with its input and output contract, tests and evaluation cases, keeping the question and context for resuming.

nodes.label: Verify and register
nodes.text: The system independently verifies the candidate query and registers a version only with the required permission, keeping failed candidates visible but unregistered.

nodes.label: Resume the original need
nodes.text: The system runs the newly registered query for the waiting question and hands the result back for comparison, so later requests can reuse it.

nodes.label: Stop a rejected build
nodes.text: The system neither registers nor runs the rejected query, keeps its failure and the original need, and returns to method selection or reports a partial or blocked result.
nodes.condition: Verification, authorization or activation fails

nodes.label: Choose the offered query
nodes.text: Jev compares the offered queries by purpose, inputs, outputs, scope and known limits and picks the one that fits the need, or decides that none fits or that it must ask.

nodes.label: Decide preparation needs
nodes.text: Jev decides how the query's inputs will be prepared, from trusted known values, model-proposed values, fact discovery or clarification, without writing them itself.

nodes.label: Bind known values or dispatch preparation
nodes.text: The kernel fills in trusted known values directly or sends the host model a request with the question, the chosen query and approved context, then waits for its reply.

nodes.label: Optionally propose arguments
nodes.text: When known values are not enough, the host model proposes the query's inputs with their basis, flagging any it cannot resolve instead of inventing IDs or facts.

nodes.label: Validate arguments and resume
nodes.text: The kernel checks the proposed inputs against the query, scope, required fields and budget, rejects invalid ones, blocks duplicate runs and routes missing facts onward.

nodes.label: Judge argument adequacy
nodes.text: Jev judges whether the valid inputs actually serve the original need and chooses to run the query, correct the inputs, discover more facts, ask or stop.

nodes.label: Execute and return evidence
nodes.text: The kernel runs the chosen query within the allowed scope and budget and returns its results, with their sources and completeness limits, for comparison with other attempts.

nodes.label: No suitable registered query
nodes.text: Jev starts governed building of a new query for a genuine query gap, or picks another permitted method, while missing data, denied access or outages stay explicit outcomes.
nodes.condition: No catalog output contract can answer the need although required data is supported

nodes.label: Choose the search approach
nodes.text: Jev picks one or more offered keyword or vector searches and any useful component filters for the original question, within the plan and the remaining budget.

nodes.label: Gather supplied or known terms
nodes.text: The kernel collects the keywords and terms the caller supplied or that are already known in permitted context, keeping track of where each one came from.

nodes.label: Decide whether terms suffice
nodes.text: Jev decides, separately for each chosen search, whether the known terms are enough or the host model should suggest more, without writing any terms itself.

nodes.label: Request optional term generation
nodes.text: When more terms are needed, the kernel sends the host model a request tied to the original question, the approved context and the chosen search, and waits for the reply.

nodes.label: Optionally generate five terms
nodes.text: The host model suggests exactly five distinct search terms for the question, which count as search vocabulary rather than facts.

nodes.label: Validate term output
nodes.text: The kernel checks that the reply holds exactly five distinct, non-empty terms and sends invalid output to correction or records it as a limitation without searching.

nodes.label: Judge term usefulness
nodes.text: Jev judges whether the suggested terms are useful for the original question and accepts them, asks for a correction, seeks clarification or stops.

nodes.label: Run separate retrieval attempts
nodes.text: The kernel runs each permitted search once and records every attempt separately with its terms, filters, sources, evidence and outcome, without combining results yet.

nodes.label: Return separate search outcomes
nodes.text: The kernel returns each search attempt with its evidence and limits to the shared comparison, keeping empty, partial, denied and failed outcomes distinct.

nodes.label: Useful terms already available — skip LLM
nodes.text: The kernel skips term generation and searches straight away with the validated known terms, or with none when the method needs none.
nodes.condition: Known terms suffice for the selected contract, or the method needs no terms

nodes.label: An attempt was unhelpful
nodes.text: The kernel passes the unhelpful outcome to the shared comparison, where Jev may pick a different method or traversal while earlier useful evidence is kept.
nodes.condition: One selected search is empty, incomplete or fails

nodes.label: Offer a scoped starting frontier
nodes.text: The kernel offers the permitted starting graph nodes and relationships or repository folders and files from the plan, each tied to a pinned source version.

nodes.label: Choose the next navigation step
nodes.text: Jev picks which observed neighbours, folders, files or excerpts to explore next for the original question, or chooses to return evidence, switch method, ask or stop.

nodes.label: Validate the selected frontier
nodes.text: The kernel checks the choice against the offered candidates, pinned version, allowed areas and limits, rejects stale or out-of-scope picks and prevents repeated or circular reads.

nodes.label: Read nodes or code locations
nodes.text: The kernel reads the selected nodes, folders or file excerpts within budget and records the path, source, location and any truncation of each read.

nodes.label: Judge progress on the question
nodes.text: Jev judges whether the returned evidence answers the original question and chooses another place to explore, a different method, returning evidence, asking or stopping.

nodes.label: Retain history and return or resume
nodes.text: The kernel saves the visited places, attempts, evidence and remaining budget, then either continues the traversal or returns the outcomes to the shared comparison.

nodes.label: Continue through observed candidates
nodes.text: The kernel goes back to choosing the next navigation step with the observed candidates, visit history and remaining budget, without starting over.
nodes.condition: Jev selected an unvisited useful frontier and budget remains

nodes.label: Switch or add a method
nodes.text: The kernel sends the outcomes to the shared comparison and back to method selection, keeping useful evidence so the next plan can use another method or both.
nodes.condition: Jev selected an alternative/complementary method after limited progress

nodes.label: No permitted next read
nodes.text: The kernel skips reading, records the outcome for the shared comparison and finishes as partial or blocked when no other useful method remains, without retrying the same read.
nodes.condition: No useful unvisited candidate remains, the budget is exhausted, or the selected read is refused

nodes.label: Clarify intent or authority
nodes.text: Jev chooses to ask a clarifying question, which is retained with the evidence and history and passes through the shared comparison before the question is sent.
nodes.condition: Observed evidence exposes a material ambiguity that cannot be resolved safely

nodes.label: Retain a decision without reading
nodes.text: The kernel skips reading and judging and goes straight to retention, keeping the existing attempts, evidence, open candidates and budget.
nodes.condition: Jev chose return, switch, clarification or stop instead of a read

nodes.label: Ask the question
nodes.text: The caller asks a question in plain words, optionally supplying keywords or known identifiers, without choosing a retrieval method.

nodes.label: Dispatch information-needs interpretation
nodes.text: The system requests one interpretation of the information needed and preserves the accepted facts, original targets and scope for retrieval.

nodes.label: Offer permitted methods and contracts
nodes.text: The kernel works out the allowed scope, sources and remaining budget and offers the available retrieval methods, queries and relevant past strategy advice.

nodes.label: Jev chooses how to answer
nodes.text: Jev picks one or more offered methods for the original question, from registered queries, searches and graph or folder navigation, or reports a capability gap or a need to ask.

nodes.label: Retrieve the evidence
nodes.text: The kernel runs each chosen method once within scope and budget, keeps useful evidence when one fails, and collects every attempt separately for comparison.

nodes.label: Compare attempts against the original question
nodes.text: Jev compares the attempts against the original question and picks a preferred one, complementary ones, a tie or none, keeping useful evidence from each.

nodes.label: Record advisory strategy decision
nodes.text: The kernel records Jev's comparison as advisory strategy memory, with the question, attempts, methods, evidence links and limits, so future planning can consult it.

nodes.label: Combine and deduplicate useful evidence
nodes.text: The kernel merges the selected evidence and removes duplicates while keeping every supporting source and keeping differing versions or scopes separately attributed.

nodes.label: Judge relevance
nodes.text: Jev orders the combined evidence by relevance to the original question without promoting incomplete coverage.

nodes.label: Return ranked evidence
nodes.text: The kernel applies Jev's order and passes the ranked evidence, with its sources and limits, to the final sufficiency check without another retrieval.

nodes.label: Jev checks what the evidence answers
nodes.text: Jev checks what the evidence actually answers and chooses to finish, retry with a changed method, continue navigating, ask a focused question or honestly stop.

nodes.label: Dispatch wording only when needed
nodes.text: When the answer needs prose, the kernel asks the host model to word it from the accepted evidence and limits, and otherwise passes the structured facts straight on.

nodes.label: Optionally formulate the answer
nodes.text: The host model writes the answer from the accepted evidence and stated limits, without inventing facts or dropping qualifications.

nodes.label: Validate response material
nodes.text: The kernel checks the drafted answer's format, citations and retained limits, sending invalid material to correction or a partial stop.

nodes.label: Accept synthesized wording when needed
nodes.text: Jev judges the drafted wording against the supplied evidence and accepts it, asks for a revision or stops.

nodes.label: Return the result
nodes.text: The kernel assembles the answer with its evidence, status, limits and follow-up references, never using unaccepted wording, and records the final outcome in strategy memory.

nodes.label: Ask only when necessary
nodes.text: Jev chooses to ask the person a clarifying question about an unresolved intent or permission, without writing the question itself.
nodes.condition: An essential intent or authority choice cannot be resolved from context

nodes.label: Try a better plan
nodes.text: Jev goes back to method selection with the gap, retained evidence and remaining budget to try a different method, changed inputs or a new navigation step, never an unchanged repeat.
nodes.condition: Evidence has a resolvable gap and budget remains

nodes.label: Return the useful partial answer
nodes.text: The kernel returns the useful partial findings and the missing facts with their sources, without claiming the answer is complete.
nodes.condition: Some evidence is useful but completeness cannot be established

nodes.label: Explain why retrieval cannot proceed
nodes.text: The kernel returns a blocked result with the actual reason, never presenting an outage or denied access as an empty success.
nodes.condition: No permitted useful alternative remains, or a non-bypassable authority/source boundary prevents progress

nodes.label: Ask a focused follow-up
nodes.text: Jev chooses to ask the person a focused follow-up about an intent or permission the evidence left open, without writing the question itself.
nodes.condition: Retrieved evidence reveals an unresolved intent or authority choice

nodes.label: Finish with an evidenced answer
nodes.text: Jev sends the answer on to the final result with its cited evidence and any remaining non-blocking limits.
nodes.condition: The requested facts are supported and deterministic completeness checks pass

nodes.label: Dispatch the focused clarification
nodes.text: The kernel sends the person a clarifying question from a fixed template, keeping the original need, sources and progress intact.
nodes.condition: An essential intent or authority choice cannot be resolved from context

nodes.label: Supply the clarification
nodes.text: The person answers the clarifying question with the missing intent or fact, which never widens what retrieval may access.
nodes.condition: An essential intent or authority choice cannot be resolved from context

nodes.label: Validate and resume
nodes.text: The kernel checks that the reply matches the open question, applies only the allowed answer, rejects stale or conflicting replies and resumes once at method selection.
nodes.condition: An essential intent or authority choice cannot be resolved from context

nodes.label: Dispatch the focused clarification
nodes.text: The kernel sends the person a focused follow-up question from a fixed template, keeping the original need, evidence and progress intact.
nodes.condition: Retrieved evidence reveals an unresolved intent or authority choice

nodes.label: Supply the clarification
nodes.text: The person answers the follow-up with the missing intent or fact, which never widens what retrieval may access.
nodes.condition: Retrieved evidence reveals an unresolved intent or authority choice

nodes.label: Validate and resume
nodes.text: The kernel checks that the reply matches the open follow-up, applies only the allowed answer and resumes at method selection with the same need, evidence and budget.
nodes.condition: Retrieved evidence reveals an unresolved intent or authority choice

nodes.label: Try another method or frontier
nodes.text: After recording the comparison, the kernel returns to method selection or the saved navigation point with the useful evidence, or stops as partial or blocked if nothing new remains.
nodes.condition: Jev selected a changed plan or observed traversal continuation and budget remains
